newsitem.title: USA: Florida jobless rate dips to 4.8 pct in February.
newsitem.headline: Florida jobless rate dips to 4.8 pct in February.

text.p: Florida's unemployment rate edged down to 4.8 percent in February from the revised rate of 4.9 percent for January, the state Department of Labor and Employment Security said Tuesday.
The February rate was Florida's lowest since May, 1988, when it also dipped to 4.8 percent. The data represent 337,000 unemployed Floridians out of a civilian workforce of 7.09 million.

Monroe County had Florida's lowest unemployment rate, 2.3 percent, and Taylor County had the highest, 9.9 percent. Of Florida's 67 counties, 51 had declines in their unemployment rate from February of last year.
Services added the most jobs, 105,600, and had the haghest growth rate, 5.1 percent, over the year.

Trade gained the second largest number of new jobs, 59,400, with strongest gains in restaurants, food stores, building materials, hardware, garden supplies and mobile home dealers. For the first time 10 months, job growth in retail trade surpassed growth in wholesale trade.
Construction grew by 6,900 jobs or 2.2 percent, while manufacturing grew by 4,800 jobs or one percent over the year.
Transportation, communications and public utilities lost 12,500 jobs, a four percent drop, mainly due to layoffs in utilities because of expected deregulation and increased competition.
Finance, insurance and real estate grew by 14,200 jobs or 3.7 percent, while government grew by 16,700 jobs or 1.8 percent.
